x: As can be seen from the result hereunder, we had the first 13 men home and so scored a hollow victory in the team race. The individual winner was Bill Lucas, and he finished full of running, and was followed home by Ches.

And so away they went on the first lap, leaving our supporters with the hope that when they reappeared that a Belgrave man would be in the lead, but it was not to be, and at the end of the first lap of 2½ miles, Eddie Short was our first man in 8th position. Ches. Walker, running well, was 20th followed by Len.

Tom Carter is still showing useful form for an old 'un, and it is to the younger element such as Mike Heard, Len Adams, Bragginton, Popplewell and Ches Walker, that we look to for support in the more serious races to come.
First man home was Ches Walker, our " novice " discovery and he ran well to beat Dunkley of the Poly, who was a member of their last year's Brighton Relay team.
Over our five miles course Field finished a good winner in 30 mins. 8 secs., and Archie Bedford ran well to finish a close second with Ches Walker also well up.

The Junior race run over two laps followed after the senior race and by this time some of the mud had been trodden down but the course was still water-logged in parts and very heavy. Ches Walker was our first man home closely followed by Mike Stearman and on such a course both these lads had run well.
The Junior event saw a field of 361 turn out and our lads were never in the first flight but Ches. Walker ran fairly well but here again Mike Stearman did not do so well as at Eastbourne.
Ches Walker, who is just 21 years of age, ran very well to gain third place and this lad should develop into a real champion in a few seasons' time.
Ches Walker, our youngest runner, went next and running in nice style he caught and passed the Aylesford runner and also gained on the other teams and his time was second fastest for this stage.
Fergusson, who has on occasions run for the A.A.A. We won the 880 yards when Ches Walker beat L.
Ches Walker was our last runner and although Peter Pirie gained 20 secs. on him, he was never in any danger of being caught, and finished a comfortable winner.
In the 1 mile it was our turn to score a “ maximum ” and we actually had the first three men home, with Jack Brown leading Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker in the good time of 4 min. 31.4 secs.

Marshall running for us, and they all ran well to come home winners in the good time of 46.9 secs. We then came to the Senior 1 mile Medley Relay, and Ches. Walker ran the 880 yds. stage and did quite well to hand over in third place.
Ches Walker ran a good race to win the 880 yards in the fast time of 2 mins. 2 secs., while Jack Brown won the 1 mile race in 4 mins. 32.3 secs.
Ches Walker ran his best mile to date when gaining third place in the 1 mile final and he beat Jimmy Wood and also gained his Southern standard, which is of 4 mins. 28 secs.
The 1,000 yards saw our real strength and here we had the first three home in Derrick Burfitt, Ches Walker and Vernon Blowfield, with Jimmy Wood, of the Poly, 4th.
Ches Walker won the 880 yards and T. Underwood was second in the 440 and Bill Lucas scored a good win over Len Herbert in the 2 miles run when clocking 9 mins. 39 secs.
Ches Walker won the 880 and Bob Taylor filled fourth place to score a point for us, but in the 440 yards Herne Hill had the first three home with Jim Heathfield first of our runners.

Thompson, the international runner, and " Mac " clocked 4 min. 33.8 secs., which is good going for a lad of his age. Ches Walker won the 440 yards, with Odde in second place, and Jack Brown won the 880, with Archie Bedford fourth.

The heats of the 1 mile saw Jack Brown and Ches Walker competing and a notable absentee was Derrick Burfitt. Brown ran quite well to finish inside the standard time of 4 min. 25 secs., and Walker also gained standard and actually finished a very close fourth in his heat with the first three only goi…
Odde was second in the quarter and Gerry Trower won the junior 880 in good style and Ches Walker was also first home in the senior half-mile.

Derrick Burfitt and Ches Walker were first and second in the 880 yards, and Bill Lucas won the 1 mile with Vern Blowfield in third place. Len Herbert won the 2 miles race in 9 min. 34.4 secs., but we were beaten in the team race by S.L.H.
Ches Walker won the 880, with Alan Bishop in fourth place, and I.

Cope, was not competing, and Ches Walker won a good race from Archie Bedford, with Len Bishop running well for third place. Frank Kemp made a double of it by winning the 220 yards Junior race, beating Dave Marshall, who is the Surrey champion at this distance.
Merrett was third in the 100 yards and Ches. Walker third in the 880, while Jack Brown finished second in the 1 mile.
Ches. Walker ran a fine race in the 1 mile off a back mark and must have run his fastest mile of the season to get through his field to win.
Gordon Lowers retained his 100 yards title in the good time of 10.6 secs, on a very heavy track, and then Ches Walker won the 1 mile in 4 mins. 28.8 secs. with Bob Taylor in second place.
Ches Walker went off first for us and he beat Stone of Dorking and Martin of Walton A.C. to give Jack Bragginton a useful lead, and his time of 14 mins. 12 secs. beat the previous course record.

Arthur Bruce was our next runner and although he did second fastest time the Reading man increased his side's lead. Jack Bragginton then went off and ran well to gain half-a-minute on the leader but our last runner, Ches Walker, had J.

Bill Lucas came next and he was followed by Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker, who came in together, with Bob Taylor and Ted Stimpson close behind, and this laid the foundation of our win in the team race over our old and friendly rivals.
Vernon, therefore, did extremely well to maintain the same lead, and when Ches Walker took over for the fifth stage we were practically certain of victory.
At the half-way mark a small bunch of runners were at the head of the field, but when they came into the finishing field Ches Walker and Len Herbert were battling it out neck-and-neck.

Stone, the holder, was leading, but Ches Walker was close behind and, moreover, was running very easily, and it was obvious that unless Stone could get away from his opponent on the second lap of the country he had had it!

Our first member to finish was Ches Walker, who ran well to finish 7th in such a high-class field, while Jack Brown also did well in finishing 34th and missed by one place being the sixth scoring man for his county, who were placed third.
We also had the individual winner in Ches. Walker and he ran in very smooth style throughout and only one other runner got anywhere near him over the very heavy 7½ miles course.
Gordon Lowers retained his 100 yards title in the good time of 10.6 secs on a very heavy track, and then Ches. Walker won the mile in 4 mins 28.8 secs. with Bob Taylor in second place.

At the half distance J.W.Stone, the holder, was leading but Ches . Walker was close behind and, moreover, was running very easily, and it was obvious that unless Stone could get away from his opponent on the second lap of the country he had had it!
